text:
maya_support: FYI customer (org: AcmeWidgets) reports a spike of 5xxs and auth failures since ~10:15 UTC. They claim requests with x-region-hint: us-west are landing in eu-west-1 and seeing ~600ms extra RT. Billing also spiked for outbound cross-region tokens :/

sam_oncall: Ack. Can you paste a sample request_id + a small request/response capture? I'll pull traces.

maya_support: request_id: rwd-0a3f94. Minimal curl they used:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "x-region-hint: us-west" \\  -H "Host: api.redwood.example" \\  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

Response headers from customer side (snipped):
x-upstream-host: eu-west-1.gw.internal
x-request-id: rwd-0a3f94
set-cookie: rw_affinity=eu-west-1; Path=/; HttpOnly

sam_oncall: Thanks. I can already see traces showing routing to cluster eu-west-1 for that request_id. Pulling envoy access logs now.

zara_eng: Quick hypothesis: we have a rewrite rule introduced in canary that normalizes rw_affinity cookie domain/path. If the gateway rewrites affinity cookie to a global domain, subsequent requests from clients can pick up the cookie value and get steered cross-region. Seen this once in A/B tests where Set-Cookie Domain=.example caused sticky to prefer eu.

ops_sre: If that's true, the symptom fits: initial request had x-region-hint us-west, but the client had an older cookie rw_affinity=eu-west-1 and envoy's cookie affinity policy wins. Need to check cookie precedence vs header steer.

maya_support: Customer says they didn't have rw_affinity before today, but their browser used our web app which may have received a set-cookie earlier from an edge canary.

zara_eng: Repro steps I used in staging:
1) curl to api with header x-region-hint:us-west -> responded and set rw_affinity=us-west
2) simulate a canary response that sets rw_affinity=eu-west-1 (we had a bad rule)
3) subsequent curl with same cookies gets routed to eu-west-1 even with x-region-hint header.

Commands I ran (staging):
```
# get cookie
curl -c /tmp/c -H "x-region-hint: us-west" https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# simulate canary set
curl -b /tmp/c -c /tmp/c --header "x-canary-test: 1" https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/debug/set-cookie?cookie=rw_affinity=eu-west-1
# now request
curl -b /tmp/c -H "x-region-hint: us-west" -v https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Observed: last request goes to eu-west-1 cluster. Expected: header steer should override cookie when present.

ops_sre: Good repro. Likely bug: our L7 routing policy gives cookie-based sticky > x-region-hint header in the case of conflicting signals. Also need to inspect Envoy config that rewrites Set-Cookie Domain/Path.

sam_oncall: For immediate mitigation: we can push a routing override that honors x-region-hint at edge (temporary precedence change) OR add a short-lived header-based shadow that sets x-force-region. I'll do a quick manual route override for AcmeWidgets and any requests with x-region-hint until this is fixed.

deploy-bot: Started rollout: route-override/priority-hint-2026-03-17 (canary -> 10%).

zara_eng: Two parallel fixes to plan: (A) revert the canary rule that set global cookie domain and (B) change routing precedence: header > cookie, and add unit tests for header+cookie conflict cases. I can cut a PR for (B) after we confirm config.

ops_sre: Action list:
- [ ] enable debug logging on edge gateway for cookie routing (sam)
- [ ] patch route override for customer and x-region-hint (sam)
- [ ] revert canary cookie rewrite (zara)
- [ ] run smoke against EU/US to validate no cross-region sticky (zara + ops_sre)

carlos_support: Escalating to incident — INCIDENT-3421 opened. Tagging legal/channel for billing spike review. @support oncall please paste cost delta and timeframe.

maya_support: Customer impact: ~2.3% of their requests hit eu-west for ~30m window; they reported 400s->5xxs for 10% of flows. Billing team pinged.

sam_oncall: I enabled debug and grabbed a sample envoy access log for rwd-0a3f94:
```
[2026-03-17T10:16:05.123Z] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 - upstream_host: eu-west-1.gw.internal rw_affinity=eu-west-1 x-region-hint=us-west route=sticky_cookie
```
Shows route=sticky_cookie. We should change that to route=region_hint for this customer.

zara_eng: Will open PR referencing INCIDENT-3421 and add tests. Quick note: also audit other cookies we write at edge (auth, session, rw_affinity) for Domain/Path flags; SameSite=None + Domain=.example was the culprit in earlier incident.

ops_sre: Temporary customer mitigation applied. We'll keep tracking and update channel. If anyone sees more orgs with cross-region traffic spike, flag here. :thumbsup:

maya_support: Customer confirmed latency dropped after we forced region for them. They want RCA and billing credit request template.

carlos_support: I'll draft billing impact note and send internal template to finance. Assigning follow-ups: zara for fix (PR), ops_sre for deploy verification, sam for debug logs/trace collection, maya for customer comms.

sam_oncall: Leaving debug on for 2h then flip to info.

zara_eng: PR created: github.com/redwood/inference/ops-config/pull/1289 -> change precedence + tests.

maya_support: Thanks all. Closing temporary escalate once PR is deployed and passing smoke.

ops_sre: Marking thread resolved for now, keeping incident open for RCA write-up.
